newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians to brief Jordan on peace efforts.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians to brief Jordan on peace efforts.

text.p: Palestinian peace negotiator Nabil Shaath said on Saturday he would visit Jordan on Sunday to brief officials there on efforts to revive Israeli-Palestinian talks.
"I am going to Jordan to inform the Jordanian leadership on the latest developments in the peace process," Shaath told Reuters.
Shaath held talks with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Wednesday on opening a Palestinian airport in the self-ruled Gaza Strip, which he said could help jump-start peace talks.
Palestinian-Israeli talks have been frozen since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Jordan's King Hussein has blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for a breakdown in the peacemaking.

"...I must admit I am very disappointed in the performance as a whole of Israel and of its government and its leadership in the present and the recent past. I really hope we will see some improvement before it is too late," Hussein told the British Broadcasting Coorporation in an interview.
Shaath called on Israel to release Palestinians jailed in Israel who are under the age of 16, over the age of 50 and those who have served two-thirds of their prison terms.
"If Israel releases such a group of prisoners as a first step it would open the way to serious negotiations on the issue of prisoners," Shaath said.

In February Israel released 30 Palestinian women from its jails under an interim deal it signed with the PLO. It has also freed some male prisoners but according to the accord it is to release additional prisoners.
Palestinian sources say some 5,000 Palestinians remain in Israeli jails.
